what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat adults with a certain type of prostate cancer that has spread to other parts of the body (metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, or mCRPC). It is specifically for patients whose tumors have a gene change called BRCA mutation. It is used together with a steroid called prednisone or methylprednisolone.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth (swallow the tablets whole — do not crush, break, or chew them). Always take it on an EMPTY STOMACH — do not eat anything for at least 2 hours before and at least 1 hour after taking your dose. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Always take it with your prescribed steroid (prednisone or methylprednisolone) as directed by your doctor. Drink a full glass of water with each dose.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 2 tablets (each tablet contains niraparib 100 mg and abiraterone 500 mg) taken once daily — for a total daily dose of niraparib 200 mg and abiraterone 1000 mg. Your doctor may lower your dose if you experience side effects. Do not change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular scheduled time. Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep away from heat, light, and moisture. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Do not eat for at least 2 hours before or 1 hour after taking this medicine — food (especially high-fat meals) can increase the amount of abiraterone absorbed into your body to unsafe levels. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they may affect how your body processes this medicine. Avoid handling crushed or broken tablets if you are pregnant or may become pregnant, as this medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not donate blood or sperm while taking this medicine and for at least 3 months after stopping. If you are a man with a pregnant partner, use effective birth control (such as a condom) during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: signs of low blood cell counts such as unusual tiredness, paleness, shortness of breath, fever, chills, or easy bruising or bleeding; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain; high blood pressure, especially sudden severe headache or vision changes; swelling in your legs or feet; chest pain or irregular heartbeat; signs of a rare blood disorder called MDS or AML such as recurring infections or very low blood counts; signs of adrenal gland problems such as extreme fatigue, weight loss, or nausea; bone or joint pain that is severe or new; falls or dizziness; any signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, or swelling.
when_it_works: This medicine begins working right away at the cellular level, but you may not feel or notice changes immediately. Your doctor will monitor your progress through regular blood tests and scans. It may take several weeks to months before your doctor can see a measurable response. Do not stop taking the medicine on your own, even if you feel well or do not notice immediate changes.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine can cause serious harm to an unborn baby and should NOT be used by women who are pregnant or breastfeeding. Men taking this medicine should use effective contraception if their partner could become pregnant. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely if you have kidney or liver disease. Older adults (65 years and older): Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects such as fatigue, falls, and blood pressure changes — talk to your doctor about any concerns. Patients with heart conditions: This medicine may affect heart rhythm and blood pressure, so your doctor will monitor your heart health regularly.
